answer: A market can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it trades, like a walnut that only cracks open after real work. A new identity starts with no history, so it cannot borrow reputation — it must earn trust one verified delivery at a time, while a raven-like monitor flags clusters of accounts that share timing and wording. A Sybil attacker then faces a cold tundra: every fake identity costs a stake and weeks of honest work, while a single fraud forfeits the whole deposit.
